pattern.top_pattern: Outside CA, acute hospital growth is coming from a mix of volume at key providers and selective price pressure
pattern.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group / ACUTE HOSPITAL / NY, OH, and NH / PPO and EPO

providers: OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER

key_driver_codes: OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY WEXNER MEDICAL CENTER
pattern.pattern_details: In NY and OH, acute hospital growth is being pushed by more PA-required admissions at major providers, while separate PPO and EPO slices show higher payment per admit even when volume is flat or down. The business lever is to separate pure utilization growth from selective reimbursement pressure by provider and auth status.
pattern.why_it_matters: This pattern supports targeted provider action at NYU and Ohio State instead of a broad marketwide response.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run provider-level action plans for NYU and Ohio State that split PA-required volume growth from non-PA price pressure, and review ungroupable and aftercare claims as separate reimbursement issues.
evidence_summary: NY PPO PA-required acute claims at NYU added +$1.8M on 19 more admissions even as paid per admit fell.
OH PPO PA-required acute claims at Ohio State added +$1.5M on 47 more admissions even as paid per admit fell.
OH and NH PPO unit-cost findings added +$1.5M, led by OH ungroupable cases with paid per admit up about $90K.
NY EPO acute aftercare added +$544K with paid per admit up about $109K.
